comments.text:
## Project Context
First foundation bead for the server. All 14 tables from docs/01-database-schema.md must be created in Drizzle ORM. This is the data layer everything else depends on.

## What to Build
- packages/server/src/db/schema.ts: 14 tables (users, projects, repos, project_members, captures, epics, sessions, session_events, agent_queue, knowledge_rules, webhook_configs, notifications, activity_log)
- packages/server/src/db/index.ts: Drizzle + better-sqlite3, pragmas (WAL, 64MB cache, FK ON, synchronous NORMAL), runMigrations(), seedAdmin()
- packages/server/src/db/test-db.ts: createTestDb() for in-memory SQLite, cleanAllTables() for test isolation
- Run drizzle-kit generate for initial migration

## Key Constraints
- All timestamps: INTEGER (unix epoch) with DEFAULT (unixepoch())
- JSON fields (git_branches, scope_analysis, triage_result, events): stored as TEXT, parsed in app
- session_events uses AUTOINCREMENT PK (not UUID) for ordering
- activity_log also uses AUTOINCREMENT
- Proper indexes per spec: (project_id, status) on captures, (project_id) on epics, etc.
- Reference: docs/01-database-schema.md for complete spec
- Reference: git show b1abceb:packages/server/src/db/schema.ts for prior implementation

title: Fix: session API calls fail with Project ID required
description:
## Context
Sending messages, resuming, cancelling sessions all fail with "Project ID required". The sessions router has requireProjectMember middleware which needs :projectId, but the client calls session-scoped URLs (/sessions/:id/resume) without a project prefix.

## Root Cause
Server mounts the same router at two paths:
- /api/projects/:projectId/sessions — project-scoped (has projectId)
- /api/sessions — session-scoped (no projectId)

The router internally uses router.use(requireProjectMember) which needs projectId on ALL routes, but session-scoped operations (get, cancel, resume, answer, events) are called via /api/sessions/:id/... where projectId is undefined.

Client resources.ts calls:
- resume: /sessions/${sessionId}/resume (no projectId)
- cancel: /sessions/${sessionId}/cancel (no projectId)
- answer: /sessions/${sessionId}/answer (no projectId)
- get: /sessions/${sessionId} (no projectId)
- events: /sessions/${sessionId}/events (no projectId)

## What to Change

### Option A (preferred — client fix):
- packages/client/src/lib/resources.ts: Change all session-scoped API methods to use project-scoped URLs: /projects/${projectId}/sessions/${sessionId}/...
- Update method signatures to accept projectId parameter
- packages/client/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts: Pass projectId (from useProject()) to all session API calls

### Option B (server fix):
- Split sessions router into project-scoped and session-scoped routers
- Session-scoped router: no requireProjectMember, look up project from session record
- More work but cleaner API design

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Resume session works without "Project ID required" error
- [ ] Cancel session works
- [ ] Answer session questions works
- [ ] Get session detail works
- [ ] Get session events works
- [ ] All session operations still verify user has project access

## Technical Notes
- The hooks already have projectId via useProject() — just need to thread it through
- Files: packages/client/src/lib/resources.ts (lines 126-145), packages/client/src/hooks/use-sessions.ts
- The second mount at /api/sessions (index.ts line 109) may need to be removed if going with Option A
close_reason: Fixed: all session API calls now use project-scoped URLs (/projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId). Removed redundant /api/sessions mount. Commit 9a0c94c.

comments.text:
## Project Context
This is the CRITICAL PATH — the core engine that makes the entire system work. It powers the Semi-Auto Execution Engine (Pillar 2). Without this, the app is just a dashboard.

## What to Build
Port playgrounds/agents/server/session-manager.ts to production with these additions:
1. Agent SDK query() with canUseTool callback, AbortController for cancellation
2. AskUserQuestion: hold canUseTool promise, resolve with answers. 3 modes (pause/auto/hybrid) per project config.
3. DB persistence: create session row, store each NDJSON event in session_events, update status on lifecycle changes
4. Queue management: check project.max_concurrent_agents, add to agent_queue if limit reached, processQueue() after session completion
5. Context building: br show for epic details, CM rules, CASS learnings, codebase snapshot
6. Crash recovery: recoverOrphanedSessions() on server start — find status=running/waiting_input, check for orphaned processes, mark as detached
7. Socket.IO integration: emit session:event, session:lifecycle, session:question, session:progress to session + project rooms
8. Pre-push validation: run tests, check build, scan for forbidden patterns (merge conflicts, console.log, test.only)

## Key Patterns from Reference
- canUseTool returns { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input } — MUST include updatedInput
- AskUserQuestion: resolve promise with { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: { ...input, answers: { q: answer } } }
- Context window: extract from assistant.message.usage (input_tokens + cache_creation + cache_read)
- Session resume: pass resume: sessionId in options

Reference: playgrounds/agents/server/session-manager.ts (629 lines), docs/06-agent-lifecycle.md (12 phases)

title: Wire Integrations section to real health diagnostics endpoint
description:
## Context
The Project Settings Integrations section shows Agent Mail, CM, and CASS with connection status indicators. Currently the "Refresh status" button shows a toast saying "not yet connected to backend." The backend GET /api/health/diagnostics endpoint already exists and returns real status for these services.

## What to Change
- **packages/client/src/components/settings/project-tab.tsx**: Replace stub `handleRefreshIntegrations()` with a real API call to `GET /api/health/diagnostics`
- **packages/client/src/lib/resources.ts**: Add `healthApi.diagnostics()` method
- Parse the diagnostics response and map to the 3 displayed services:
  - Agent Mail → `dockerServices.agentMail` status
  - Context Manager (CM) → `dockerServices.cm` status
  - CASS → `cliTools.cass` status
- Update status indicators (green=connected, red=disconnected, yellow=not-found) based on real response
- Load integration status on component mount, not just on button click

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Refresh button calls GET /api/health/diagnostics and updates status indicators
- [ ] Status loads automatically when the settings tab opens
- [ ] Only Agent Mail, CM, and CASS are shown (not other CLI tools)
- [ ] Error states handled gracefully (toast on network failure)
- [ ] Loading spinner shown while fetching

## Technical Notes
- Backend endpoint requires authentication + techlead role (see routes/health.ts)
- Response shape: `{ cliTools: { cass: { available, version?, path? } }, dockerServices: { agentMail: { status, url }, cm: { status, url } } }`

title: Implement project image upload with Cloudflare R2 storage
description:
## Context
The Project Identity section in settings has Upload/Remove buttons for a project picture. Currently they just show toast notifications. Need full image upload pipeline with Cloudflare R2 as storage backend.

## What to Change

### Backend (packages/server/)
- **db/schema.ts**: Add `picture_url` TEXT column to projects table
- **Generate migration**: `pnpm db:generate` after schema change
- **services/r2-service.ts**: New service wrapping Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible API via @aws-sdk/client-s3)
  - `upload(key, buffer, contentType)` → returns public URL
  - `delete(key)` → removes object
  - Bucket/credentials from env vars: `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_BUCKET_NAME`, `R2_PUBLIC_URL`
- **routes/projects.ts**: Add `POST /api/projects/:projectId/picture` (multipart upload via multer)
  - Validate file type (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp) and max size (2MB)
  - Upload to R2 with key: `projects/{projectId}/picture.{ext}`
  - Update project record with `picture_url`
  - Emit socket event `project:updated`
- **routes/projects.ts**: Add `DELETE /api/projects/:projectId/picture`
  - Delete from R2, set `picture_url` to null
  - Emit socket event `project:updated`
- **Add multer dependency**: `pnpm add multer @types/multer` in packages/server

### Frontend (packages/client/)
- **lib/resources.ts**: Add `projectsApi.uploadPicture(projectId, file)` and `projectsApi.removePicture(projectId)`
- **components/settings/project-tab.tsx**: Wire Upload button to file input + upload mutation, Remove button to delete mutation
  - Show uploaded image in avatar instead of initials
  - Loading state during upload
  - Preview before upload (optional)

### Environment
- Add R2 env vars to `.env.example`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Upload button opens file picker, accepts PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 2MB
- [ ] Image uploads to R2 and URL is persisted in project record
- [ ] Project avatar shows uploaded image instead of initials
- [ ] Remove button deletes from R2 and reverts to initials avatar
- [ ] File type and size validation with user-friendly error messages
- [ ] Socket event emitted so other clients see the update in real-time

## Technical Notes
- R2 is S3-compatible — use @aws-sdk/client-s3 with custom endpoint
- multer memoryStorage for buffer access before R2 upload
- Recommended 256x256px per UI hint — consider server-side resize with sharp (optional)
- Role restriction: PM and TechLead only (requireRole middleware)

title: Hybrid Agent Auth: seed bot user and thread API keys to sessions
description:
## Context
Agent sessions need to call server REST APIs (e.g., /triage skill calls PATCH /captures). 
Decision: user-triggered sessions use the starting user's API key, background tasks use a dedicated agent-bot user's key.
See .ccu/DECISIONS.md and history/2026-03-27-draft-hybrid-agent-auth/approach.md.

## Scope
1. Seed an agent-bot user with dev role and dedicated API key
2. Fetch user's api_key in session runner when picking up queued sessions
3. Pass CTW_* env vars to Agent SDK query() via the env option
4. Add CTW_BOT_API_KEY to .env.example

title: Implement webhook test messages and dispatch for Discord/Telegram
description:
## Context
Webhook CRUD (create/update/delete) works, but two things are broken/missing:
1. "Send Test" button only shows a toast — no actual HTTP request to the webhook URL
2. No webhook dispatch service — events (session_complete, pr_ready, etc.) never trigger webhook delivery

## What to Change

### Backend (packages/server/)
- **routes/webhooks.ts**: Add POST /:webhookId/test endpoint
  - Fetch webhook config from DB
  - Format a test payload appropriate to the webhook type (Discord embed, Telegram message, Slack block)
  - POST to the webhook URL
  - Return success/failure with HTTP status from the target
- **services/webhook-dispatcher.ts**: New service
  - formatDiscordPayload(event, data) — Discord embed format
  - formatTelegramPayload(event, data) — Telegram sendMessage format
  - formatSlackPayload(event, data) — Slack block kit format
  - dispatch(webhookConfig, event, data) — POST to URL with formatted payload
  - Called from session lifecycle events, PR events, etc.
- **Integration points**: Hook into session:lifecycle, pr:event emitters to trigger dispatch

### Frontend (packages/client/)
- **components/settings/webhooks-tab.tsx**: Replace stubbed handleSendTest (line 326-328) with actual API call
  - Add webhooksApi.sendTest(projectId, webhookId) to resources.ts
  - Show loading state on Send Test button
  - Show success/error toast with actual result

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Send Test button sends a real HTTP request to the webhook URL
- [ ] Discord webhooks receive properly formatted embed messages
- [ ] Telegram webhooks receive properly formatted messages via Bot API
- [ ] Success/failure feedback shown to user after test send
- [ ] Webhook URLs validated (HTTPS only, domain whitelist already exists)

## Technical Notes
- Discord webhook format: POST with { embeds: [{ title, description, color, fields }] }
- Telegram format: POST to https://api.telegram.org/bot{token}/sendMessage with { chat_id, text, parse_mode }
- Slack format: POST with { blocks: [...] }
- URL whitelist already exists in webhooks.ts (hooks.slack.com, discord.com, discordapp.com, api.telegram.org)
- Server-side fetch only — never expose webhook URLs to the client

title: Fix: sessions stuck in Queued — no agent runner to execute them
description:
## Context
When creating a new agent session, it gets status 'queued' but never transitions to 'running'. The UI shows "1 active, max 3 concurrent" indicating capacity is available, but the session stays queued. There is no agent runner/worker process that picks up queued sessions and starts Claude Code via the Agent SDK.

## Root Cause
The POST /sessions endpoint creates sessions with status='queued' but no background process exists to:
1. Poll for queued sessions
2. Start Claude Code via @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query()
3. Stream events back and update session status to 'running'
4. Handle completion/failure and update status

The playgrounds/agents/ has a working reference for the Agent SDK integration, but the server has no equivalent session runner.

## What to Change

### packages/server/src/services/session-runner.ts — New service
- Poll or subscribe for sessions with status='queued'
- For each queued session:
  1. Update status to 'running'
  2. Start Agent SDK query() with session.prompt, session.model, AbortController
  3. Stream events: insert into session_events table, emit via Socket.IO
  4. Handle canUseTool callback for tool permissions based on session permission_mode
  5. Handle AskUserQuestion: emit session:question, wait for answer via Socket.IO
  6. On completion: update status to 'completed', set finished_at
  7. On error: update status to 'failed', store error
- Respect concurrency limits (max_concurrent_agents per project)
- Reference: playgrounds/agents/ for Agent SDK patterns

### packages/server/src/index.ts — Start the runner
- Initialize SessionRunner on server startup
- Graceful shutdown: abort running sessions on SIGTERM

### Integration with existing routes
- POST /sessions/:id/cancel: AbortController.abort() on the running session
- POST /sessions/:id/answer: Resolve pending AskUserQuestion promise
- POST /sessions/:id/permission-mode: Update canUseTool behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Queued sessions automatically transition to 'running' within seconds
- [ ] Agent SDK streams events that appear in the session detail view
- [ ] Session completes and status updates to 'completed' or 'failed'
- [ ] Concurrency limits respected (no more than max_concurrent_agents running per project)
- [ ] Cancel button aborts the running agent
- [ ] Questions from agent are surfaced to the UI for user to answer

## Technical Notes
- Agent SDK: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() with AbortController
- canUseTool callback MUST return { behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input } (see CLAUDE.md)
- AskUserQuestion: hold canUseTool promise, resolve when answer arrives
- Session resume: pass resume: sessionId in options (UUID from system.init event)
- Reference implementation: playgrounds/agents/src/ — has working patterns for all of this
- This is the most critical missing piece — without it, the entire agents feature is non-functional

comments.author: trungtran
comments.text: Reopened: Two new issues found. (1) Agent sessions don't load project skills, commands, or agents — the session runner likely doesn't configure Claude Code with the project's .claude/ directory. (2) Agent sessions MUST run in the specific repository directory (not packages/server/), and the target directory should be a required user input when creating a session. The session runner needs: a targetDir parameter passed from session creation, and to spawn Claude Code with cwd set to that directory so skills and project context load correctly.

title: De-stub Improve with AI using Agent SDK for rule improvement
description:
## Context
The CM rules "Add Rule" dialog has an "Improve with AI" button (Sparkles icon) that currently uses a hardcoded setTimeout with mock suggestions. Need to replace with a real Agent SDK call that improves rule text quality.

## What to Change

### Backend (packages/server/)
- **routes/rules.ts**: Add `POST /api/projects/:projectId/rules/improve` endpoint
  - Accepts: `{ text: string }` (the raw rule text to improve)
  - Returns: `{ suggestion: string, explanation: string, category: string }`
  - Use Agent SDK `query()` with a focused prompt:
    - System: "You are a knowledge rule editor for AI coding agents. Improve the given rule to be more specific, actionable, and imperative. Return JSON with suggestion, explanation, and suggested category."
    - User: the raw rule text
  - AbortController with 15s timeout
  - Parse structured response from Claude
  - Role: any authenticated user (PM, Dev, TechLead)

### Frontend (packages/client/)
- **components/settings/rules-tab.tsx**: Replace `handleImproveWithAI()` stub
  - Remove hardcoded `aiImprovements` mock data (lines 52-59)
  - Remove setTimeout simulation (lines 95-106)
  - Call `POST /api/projects/:projectId/rules/improve` with current rule text
  - Display real suggestion, explanation, and category from response
  - Handle loading, error, and empty-text states
- **lib/resources.ts**: Add `rulesApi.improve(projectId, text)` method

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking "Improve with AI" sends rule text to backend and shows real AI suggestion
- [ ] AI suggestion panel shows improved text, explanation of changes, and suggested category
- [ ] Accept button replaces rule text with AI suggestion and updates category dropdown
- [ ] Dismiss button clears the suggestion
- [ ] Loading spinner shown during API call
- [ ] Error toast on failure (network error, timeout)
- [ ] Button disabled when rule text is empty
- [ ] No hardcoded mock data remains

## Technical Notes
- Reference: playgrounds/agents/ for Agent SDK patterns
- Agent SDK usage: `query()` with structured prompt, parse JSON from response
- Keep the prompt focused — this is a single-turn improvement, not a conversation
- 15s timeout is generous; most improvements should return in 3-5s
- Consider caching recent improvements to avoid redundant calls on the same text
close_reason: Implemented POST /rules/improve with Agent SDK. Frontend wired, mock data removed. Commit 3a1f94b.

title: De-stub Triage: real agent session with /triage skill as initial prompt
description:
## Context
The Triage feature in captures page uses a TriageDialog with hardcoded simulated questions and results. It should start a REAL Agent session that runs the /triage skill, streams results back, and creates actual epics/beads from triage output.

## What to Change

### components/capture/triage-dialog.tsx — Replace simulation with real agent session
- Remove all simulated data: simulatedQuestions (lines 46-59), simulatedTriageResult (lines 62-75)
- Remove setTimeout-based simulation (lines 77-83)
- On "Start Triage": create a real agent session via `useCreateSessionMutation()` with prompt set to the /triage skill invocation and selected capture IDs as context
- Stream session events in the dialog using `useSessionEventsQuery()` or Socket.IO
- When agent asks questions (session:question events), display them in the dialog's question phase
- When agent completes, parse the triage result (beads created, classifications) and show in completion phase

### Backend integration
- Session creation should include capture context: the selected capture texts passed as part of the prompt
- The prompt should instruct the agent to triage the provided captures using the /triage skill pattern
- Triage results (bead IDs, classifications) should be extractable from session events

### captures-page.tsx — Wire triage completion
- On triage complete, update capture statuses to 'triaged' with real bead references
- Navigate to created epic/bead if user clicks "View Epic"

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Selecting captures and clicking "Triage" starts a real Claude Code agent session
- [ ] Agent session uses /triage skill pattern as initial prompt with capture context
- [ ] Agent questions are displayed in the triage dialog for user to answer
- [ ] Triage results show real beads/epics created by the agent
- [ ] Capture statuses updated to 'triaged' with bead references after completion
- [ ] "Start Agent Session" button creates a followup session tied to the created epic
- [ ] No simulated/hardcoded data remains in the dialog

## Technical Notes
- The /triage skill reads .ccu/CAPTURES.md and processes unchecked items
- Agent session prompt should include the specific capture texts being triaged, not just "run /triage"
- Session events can be streamed via Socket.IO (session:event) for real-time progress
- The dialog phases (review → processing → question → complete) map well to agent session lifecycle
- Backend session creation: POST /api/projects/:projectId/sessions with epicId optional
close_reason: Replaced simulated triage with real Agent SDK sessions. Captures are passed as context to the agent. Events stream live, questions handled via AskUserQuestion. Commit 83d5f1d.
